newsitem.title: GHANA: Ivory Coast says two gas lines to Ghana possible.
newsitem.headline: Ivory Coast says two gas lines to Ghana possible.

text.p: A proposed gas pipeline from Ivory Coast to a new power plant in Ghana would be the best way kick-start a regional West Africa gas link-up, Ivorian energy minister Lamine Fadika said on Friday
"Within ten years we could have our regional (gas) network," Mines and Energy Minister Lamine Fadika said at the sidelines of a three-day energy conference in Accra.

Nigeria and Ivory Coast are competing to supply 30 million cubic feet/day of gas to a new power station at Takoradi coming on stream in 1997 but proposals should be seen as complimentary, he said on the last day of Africa Oil and Gas 1997.
A proposed regional pipeline would take gas to Ghana, Ivory Coast, Benin, Togo as well as the rest of Nigeria.

Bids submitted to Ghana's Volta River Authority (VRA) include plans for a 640 km pipeline to Takoradi from Nigeria's Escravos gas field and a shorter 200 km line from more recent gas producer Ivory Coast's Kudu field.

"The Ivorian plan would allow the regional plan to develop. Then we make the connection to Nigeria which will become the largest regional supplier," adding that a regional gas network should begin with the smallest stage.

"(The pipelines) should not be seen as opposed. Both should go ahead but we must see which best fits in terms of an economic timetable," said Fadika at the conference on "Meeting Africa's Growing Oil and Gas Needs."

Ivory Coast signed two separate offshore gas production contracts last week, with U.S.-based United Meridian International Corporation (UMIC) and Houston-based Apache and is keen to develop electricity and gas export markets in Ghana.
In February, Nigeria signed a letter of intent to supply natural gas to Ghana via a pipeline through Benin and Togo.
The letter covered an agreement between Chevron and Ghana National Petroleum for supplying gas for VRA's Takoradi plant.
A wider plan for a West Africa Gas Pipeline would include supplying five countries with a total of 280 million cubic feet/day of eastern Nigerian natural gas from Escravos.
Nigeria flares an estimated 75 percent of its oil-associated natural gas.

Fadika said Ivory Coast would promote the idea of a "regional energy pool" and the setting up of a West African Oil and Gas Conference. A regional network would eventually be extended to Guinea, Mali and Burkina Faso, he said.
"If Ghana buys (Ivorian gas) we will give it priority over the Kudu ... and Foxtrot (offshore gas fields)," he added.
A decision on a tender issued by VRA two months ago is on April 17 but bidders expect delays as private consultant Arthur D.Little was still reviewing options.

Delegates said pipeline bidders included United Meridian International Corp (UMIC), Shell International, Chevron together with Ghana National Petroleum Corporation, Titan Projects of Canada and Vermeer Contractors Group of The Netherlands.

Ghana's Volta River Authority signed a $70 million deal for a Takoradi power station steam turbine with U.S.-based General Electric on Thursday to expand capacity at Takoradi from 200 MW in late 1997 to 300 MW in 1998.
